title: A function continuous at every point of a compact set and vanishing off it is integrable
statement: Let n be a natural number, F : R^n → R and K ⊆ R^n compact. Assume F is continuous at every point of K and F(x) = 0 for every x ∉ K. Then F is Lebesgue integrable on R^n.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Rn n → ℝ) (K : Set (Rn n)), IsCompact K → (∀ x ∈ K, ContinuousAt F x) → (∀ x, x ∉ K → F x = 0) → Integrable F
